findings.description: The required manifest_files equality check is bypassed when arm_evidence omits manifest_files or supplies an empty value. The nonempty guard makes incomplete evidence pass integrity_clean.
findings.failure_mode: Failure: when a home-scope run has an otherwise valid integrity record but no manifest_files evidence, then integrity_clean reports success without establishing the required equality between the record's file count and arm_evidence.
findings.suggested_fix: Require manifest_files to be present and a positive integer, then require its value to equal hn; fail with explicit evidence when it is missing or malformed.
findings.demotion_reason: Demoted: anchor not in diff scope
findings.failure_scenario: Failure: when a home-scope run has an otherwise valid integrity record but no manifest_files evidence, then integrity_clean reports success without establishing the required equality between the record's file count and arm_evidence.

findings.description: The pin is normalized to a full 40-hex id via `git rev-parse -q --verify "$pin^{commit}"`, but pipeline.json's `source_commit` (`$sc`) is used raw in the equality `[[ "$c" == "$sc" ]]`. `operator_pin` accepts 7–40 hex, and `$sc` is only probed with `cat-file -e` (which accepts any resolvable rev, including abbreviations). The two sides are therefore compared in different normal forms.
findings.failure_mode: Failure: when a driver writes an abbreviated (or otherwise non-canonical but resolvable) `source_commit` into meta/pipeline.json while the operator pin names the same commit, then integrity_clean FAILs with 'the pin … is not pipeline.json source_commit …' although both name one commit, and when `$sc` is empty the probe loop emits the misleading 'source_commit <none> is in no source repository' instead of naming the missing record field.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve `$sc` the same way as the pin (`sc="$(git -C "$repo" rev-parse -q --verify "$sc^{commit}")"`) before the equality, or require `$sc` to match `^[0-9a-f]{40}$` up front and FAIL with a 'pipeline.json source_commit is not a full commit id' message.
findings.failure_scenario: Failure: when a driver writes an abbreviated (or otherwise non-canonical but resolvable) `source_commit` into meta/pipeline.json while the operator pin names the same commit, then integrity_clean FAILs with 'the pin … is not pipeline.json source_commit …' although both name one commit, and when `$sc` is empty the probe loop emits the misleading 'source_commit <none> is in no source repository' instead of naming the missing record field.

findings.description: The header for cycle-134 C-3 states 'files = arm_evidence manifest_files' as a required equality, but the implementation only checks `[[ -n "$mf" && "$mf" != "$hn" ]]`, i.e. an absent or empty `manifest_files` evidence line is accepted silently. The record/evidence equality the design relies on is thus optional in practice.
findings.failure_mode: Failure: when arm_evidence omits `manifest_files` (or a driver regression stops emitting it), then integrity_clean PASSes with the 'pin … = source_commit' evidence even though the record-to-evidence file-count binding the header promises was never checked.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat a missing/empty `manifest_files` as a FAIL ('arm_evidence has no manifest_files') or, if older runs must stay evaluable, say so explicitly in the header and append 'manifest_files: absent' to EVID so the weaker mode is visible.
findings.failure_scenario: Failure: when arm_evidence omits `manifest_files` (or a driver regression stops emitting it), then integrity_clean PASSes with the 'pin … = source_commit' evidence even though the record-to-evidence file-count binding the header promises was never checked.

findings.description: The new phases-completeness rule is driven entirely by `"$(expected_labels)"` passed as argv[7]. A command substitution in argument position never affects the caller's exit status under `set -e`, so if `expected_labels` fails (jq error, unbound variable, unexpected suite shape) the Python side receives an empty string, `want_labels` is `[]`, `missing_labels` is `[]`, and the 'phases: incomplete record' check becomes vacuous without any evidence that it was skipped.
findings.failure_mode: Failure: when `expected_labels` exits non-zero or prints nothing for an arm whose suite does declare phases, then a pipeline.json listing no or fewer phases passes clause (g)'s completeness rule silently, and the (g) evidence gives no hint that the expected-label list was empty.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture the labels first (`labels="$(expected_labels)" || { EVID="the suite's phase labels did not compute"; return 1; }`), and have the Python emit `expected=<n>` in the (g) evidence (or FAIL when `want_labels` is empty but pipeline.json lists phases) so a vacuous check is visible.
findings.failure_scenario: Failure: when `expected_labels` exits non-zero or prints nothing for an arm whose suite does declare phases, then a pipeline.json listing no or fewer phases passes clause (g)'s completeness rule silently, and the (g) evidence gives no hint that the expected-label list was empty.

findings.description: The bash side selects `$repo` with `git -C "$c" cat-file -e` and `rev-parse` under the invoking user's normal git configuration, while the Python side re-reads the same commit with `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` and `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`. Any configuration the probe depended on (notably `safe.directory` for a checkout owned by another uid, common in CI containers, or an alternates/credential-free setup) is absent for the blob read, so the two steps can disagree on the same repository.
findings.failure_mode: Failure: when the source repository is accepted by the bash probe only because of a global `safe.directory` (or similar) entry, then `git cat-file blob <sc>:.claude/checksums.json` fails in the stripped environment and integrity_clean FAILs with the misleading 'the pin … has no .claude/checksums.json files map in <repo>' although the pin's manifest exists.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one git environment for both steps: either run the bash probe/rev-parse with the same stripped `env -i`-style settings, or pass through the operator's config to the Python call (keep `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, drop the config overrides), and distinguish 'git could not read the commit' from 'no files map' in the message.
findings.failure_scenario: Failure: when the source repository is accepted by the bash probe only because of a global `safe.directory` (or similar) entry, then `git cat-file blob <sc>:.claude/checksums.json` fails in the stripped environment and integrity_clean FAILs with the misleading 'the pin … has no .claude/checksums.json files map in <repo>' although the pin's manifest exists.

findings.description: The PASS evidence embeds up to ten `extra` file names from the retained HOME verbatim (`",".join(extra[:10])`), and the hook rule embeds raw `hook_name`/query strings from transcripts in FAIL messages and in the `hooks:` evidence tail (`hook_bad`, the n==0 fail, `hook_ev`). The agent under test writes freely under its own `~/.claude/`, so it controls those file names (length up to 255 bytes each, any byte except NUL including newline, tab, ';' and ',' — the separators the evidence format itself uses). Existing fail() sites truncate transcript-derived strings (`[:80]`, `[:200]`); these new sites do not.
findings.failure_mode: Failure: when the agent creates a file such as `~/.claude/x\nintegrity_clean PASS …` or a 255-byte name repeated ten times, then EVID for integrity_clean becomes multi-line or several KiB and a line- or separator-based consumer of the took-effect report mis-parses or displays forged evidence text; the same applies to a hook name carrying control characters in the (g) evidence.
findings.suggested_fix: Sanitize untrusted names before embedding: replace control characters/separators (e.g. `re.sub(r"[\x00-\x1f;,]", "?", s)`), cap each to ~80 chars and the joined list to a fixed length, and apply the same to `hn`/`q` in the hook messages and `hook_ev` entries.
findings.failure_scenario: Failure: when the agent creates a file such as `~/.claude/x\nintegrity_clean PASS …` or a 255-byte name repeated ten times, then EVID for integrity_clean becomes multi-line or several KiB and a line- or separator-based consumer of the took-effect report mis-parses or displays forged evidence text; the same applies to a hook name carrying control characters in the (g) evidence.
